themes.consensus_view: Most desks now expect the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates at the September meeting after hotter inflation and payrolls data, while Scotiabank and State Street argue a hike is the wrong response and would be a mistake.

facts_agreed.claim: Desks have shifted their base case from the Fed holding rates to the Fed raising them.
evidence_quotes: we have changed our call: we now expect a 25bp increase to 3.75–4.00%.
We now expect the FOMC to deliver a second 25bp hike in October
the prospect of a global tightening cycle is certainly taking shape.

facts_agreed.claim: The tightening is treated as a global cycle, not a US-only move, with the Bank of Japan also seen speeding up.
evidence_quotes: the prospect of a global tightening cycle is certainly taking shape.
growing consensus that the BoJ could be set to speed up its hiking pace

facts_contested.claim: whether the Fed should hike at all
facts_contested.for_evidence: We now expect the FOMC to deliver a second 25bp hike in October
facts_contested.against_evidence: I believe that hiking would be policy error. It isn’t what the Fed should be doing.

themes.consensus_view: Most banks say the money going into AI chips and data centers is still rising and that companies are finally putting AI into real production use, while a smaller group argues the buildout is being financed too loosely and has yet to show up as economy-wide productivity or profit.

facts_agreed.claim: AI has moved from testing and pilots into production deployment at enterprises.
evidence_quotes: AI is increasingly moving from experimentation to implementation
AI adoption is moving from experimentation to measurable implementation
Enterprises are increasingly moving AI workloads into production and treating compute as a strategic resource.
software demand remains stable; AI adoption is accelerating from pilots to production deployment
Agentic AI is likely no different. The greatest opportunities will come not necessarily to those who simply adopt first

facts_agreed.claim: The AI spending cycle is not ending and demand for compute still exceeds available supply.
evidence_quotes: We believe it's too early to conclude that AI capex cycle is ending.
demand continuing to outstrip supply and bottlenecks increasingly around power, land and datacenter capacity
We see no imminent sign of the capex downturn being priced into Tech hardware.
Together, these results suggest AI infrastructure demand is not yet rolling over.
We are clearly in an AI Capex boom.

facts_agreed.claim: The binding constraint on AI buildout is physical — power, land, construction and deployment — not a shortage of demand.
evidence_quotes: Most infrastructure companies described long-duration bottlenecks around power, construction and deployment
For the first time in three decades, global electricity demand is rising faster than economic output
demand continuing to outstrip supply and bottlenecks increasingly around power, land and datacenter capacity

facts_agreed.claim: First evidence of AI paying back is appearing in company revenue and cash flow.
evidence_quotes: we are seeing increasing signs of successful AI monetization and early evidence of improving/positive ROI
AI infrastructure is moving from capital expenditure… …to cash flow.

facts_contested.claim: sustainability of the AI buildout and how it is financed
facts_contested.for_evidence: We believe it's too early to conclude that AI capex cycle is ending.
facts_contested.against_evidence: The frantic, unsustainable (in our opinion) sprint of the AI buildout should collide with unyielding brick walls

facts_contested.claim: whether AI spending has produced measurable returns yet
facts_contested.for_evidence: early evidence of improving/positive ROI on AI investments is emerging
facts_contested.against_evidence: scant evidence yet of economy-wide productivity gains

facts_contested.claim: whether markets are already pricing a spending downturn
facts_contested.for_evidence: We see no imminent sign of the capex downturn being priced into Tech hardware.
facts_contested.against_evidence: Credit is beginning to price the cost and execution risk of the AI buildout

themes.consensus_view: Banks agree that Middle East supply losses have pushed oil back above $100 and are now the main force lifting inflation and bond yields, and no desk in this set argues the squeeze is close to over.

facts_agreed.claim: Lost Middle East energy supply is a prolonged shock, not a brief scare, and it is pushing inflation high enough to force central banks to tighten.
evidence_quotes: The Iran war is no longer a short-lived energy supply shock, but a prolonged, unpredictable test
Crude oil drives inflation, and if it starts getting into the system it’s going to be hard to contain it
The further escalation of the conflict in the Persian Gulf... mean that our late-August call... looks too optimistic

facts_agreed.claim: Energy has become the dominant driver of rates and of positioning flows rather than a sector story.
evidence_quotes: The beta of front end rates to energy is back to the highs
energy was the dominant driver of the boost in overall open interest

facts_agreed.claim: The shortage extends past oil into commodities generally as buyers shift from lean inventories to stockpiling.
evidence_quotes: the world is leaving just-in-time and entering hoarding

facts_agreed.claim: Desks across the corpus flag rising energy costs as the pressure point reaching inflation, retail spending and manufacturing inputs.
evidence_quotes: Energy price pressure on inflation
Diesel as real-economy pressure point
Energy sector supply shortages
Rising manufacturing input prices
gas price impact on retail

themes.consensus_view: Banks across many desks flag the shutdown of Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline as a live supply disruption tied to attacks, but none has staked out a directional view on where oil prices go from here.

facts_agreed.claim: Multiple banks reference the shutdown of Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline as a live oil supply disruption this window.
evidence_quotes: Saudi East-West pipeline shutdown
Saudi East-West pipeline closure
Saudi Arabia east-west pipeline closure
Saudi East-West pipeline supply disruption
Saudi Arabia oil supply disruption

facts_agreed.claim: Several banks attribute the pipeline outage to attacks on Saudi oil infrastructure.
evidence_quotes: Saudi Arabia oil pipeline attacks
Houthi attack on Saudi pipeline
Saudi East-West pipeline attacks
Saudi Arabia pipeline drone attack
